page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.large is an entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the General Purpose ecs.u1 family. It is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 vCPUs derived from 1 dedicated physical core via hyperthreading, alongside 2.0 GB of memory (providing 1.0 GB per vCPU). The hardware profile includes AVX and AVX-512F instruction sets, AES cryptography support, 33 MB of L3 cache, and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest single-thread capabilities and constrained multi-threaded capacity due to the low core count. While single-threaded gzip compression reached 27.73 GB/sec and stress-ng single-core performance registered within average ranges at 1834.58, multi-core and memory-heavy benchmarks placed in the bottom tiers. Specifically, multi-core stress-ng reached 1918.98, PassMark CPU yielded 2716.28, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth capped at 15.64 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput achieved 1.91 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 2.56 GB/sec.

Given its minimal 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and the lack of local disk storage, the ecs.u1-c1m1.large represents an economical entry point for lightweight services. It is not configured for resource-intensive data processing or enterprise databases. The server is suited for lightweight workloads such as basic microservices, utility nodes, low-traffic web endpoints, small proxy services, and dev/test environments that operate within a strict 2 GB memory footprint.
